input: Draft a house rules list for new flatmates

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which areas of shared living to cover (cleaning, guests, noise, bills, kitchen, etc.) determines how comprehensive or focused the list needs to be.
The number of flatmates and their relationship to the user (strangers, friends, mixed) affects the tone — formal rules vs. friendly agreements.
The type of property and living setup (e.g. ensuite rooms, shared bathrooms, shared kitchen only) shapes which rules are actually relevant.
Whether there are existing landlord rules, tenancy clauses, or legal requirements that must be reflected changes what needs to be included.
The desired tone — strict and formal vs. relaxed and friendly — fundamentally changes the language and framing of every rule.
Understanding whether the goal is a quick reference list, a signed agreement, or a conversation-starter changes the depth and format of the output.
The intended format (printed document, group chat message, shared doc, etc.) and length affect how the rules should be structured and presented.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a house rules list for new flatmates
gold.taskDescription: Create a written set of house rules to share with new flatmates moving into a shared living space.

questions.title: Which areas of home life should the rules cover?
questions.description: Identify which topics to include — e.g. cleaning rotas, noise curfews, guests, kitchen use, bills, shared supplies — so the list is neither too narrow nor bloated.

questions.title: How many flatmates are moving in, and do you know them?
questions.description: Clarify the number of people and whether they are strangers, friends, or mixed, as this affects how personal or formal the rules should feel.

questions.title: What spaces are shared versus private in the flat?
questions.description: Determine which rooms and facilities are communal (kitchen, bathrooms, living room, garden) to ensure rules only address genuinely shared spaces.

questions.title: Are there existing landlord or tenancy rules to incorporate?
questions.description: Find out if there are lease-level restrictions (e.g. no pets, no smoking indoors) that must be reflected or referenced in the house rules.

questions.title: Should the tone be strict and formal, or relaxed and friendly?
questions.description: Establish the voice and framing — whether rules are presented as firm expectations or as a casual, collaborative agreement between housemates.

questions.title: Is this meant to be signed, or just a reference document?
questions.description: Clarify the intended use — a casual reference list, a conversation-starter for a house meeting, or a signed agreement — which changes how detailed and binding the language needs to be.

questions.title: Where will you share this — printed, digital doc, or group chat?
questions.description: Know the delivery format so the rules can be laid out appropriately, whether as a tidy numbered list, a formatted document, or a concise plain-text message.
